epistemic_rule: Random selection chooses what to study, never what is true.

hypotheses.title: Typed multi-plane dependency identity
hypotheses.claim: ClayCode package/build reproducibility is best represented by multiple linked typed identities/receipts rather than one monolithic lock hash.
falsifiers: A simpler identity scheme achieves equal semantic mutation sensitivity, equal provenance stability and equal auditability on production ClayCode cases.
Typed separation creates unresolved ambiguity that cannot be repaired without duplicating semantics.

hypotheses.title: Exact graph needs digest-bound logical package identity
hypotheses.claim: Exact versions alone are insufficient; a resolved graph must bind logical package coordinates/namespaces, exact versions or revisions, content digests and semantic dependency edges.
falsifiers: Production ecosystem guarantees immutable version-to-content binding strongly enough that digest binding adds no discriminating value under the threat model.
Content digest plus coordinate is insufficient to reproduce semantically relevant metadata/edges.

hypotheses.title: Build projection is separate from resolved graph
hypotheses.claim: Target, enabled features/groups, cfg/environment markers and other semantically active build switches need a BuildProjectionId layered above the exact resolved graph.
falsifiers: ClayCode package semantics prove target/feature-independent for all supported module forms.
Target/feature changes are already fully encoded by distinct resolved graph nodes/edges so a separate projection identity is redundant.

hypotheses.title: Logical source namespace differs from fetch locator
hypotheses.claim: A logical package source/namespace may be identity-relevant, but a transport mirror/fetch URL should not change semantic build identity when coordinate and verified content are identical.
falsifiers: Mirror/location choice changes package semantics or dependency metadata after digest verification.
ClayCode deliberately defines transport origin as part of semantic package identity for policy reasons.

hypotheses.title: Freshness/trust is admissibility, not semantic identity
hypotheses.claim: Yank/revocation/freshness/trust-root changes should be able to turn an install/build from admissible to inadmissible without rewriting the ResolvedGraphId of the already identified program.
falsifiers: Project semantics explicitly define trust status as an observable program-semantic input.
Separating trust permits replay/install of disallowed code without an enforceable policy gate.

hypotheses.title: Resolver algorithm is provenance when exact graph agrees
hypotheses.claim: Resolver algorithm/version/policy and registry resolution inputs belong in ResolutionReceipt; if two resolvers produce the same exact graph, the executable dependency graph identity should remain equal.
falsifiers: Resolver choice changes hidden semantically relevant state not represented in the graph/projection.
Audit requires resolver identity in every downstream semantic cache key for correctness, not merely provenance.

hypotheses.title: Dependency declaration never grants authority
hypotheses.claim: A package may declare required effects/capabilities, but package membership or manifest metadata must never mint runtime authority; explicit external capability grant remains mandatory.
falsifiers: None within current owner-fixed safety architecture; only an explicit project architecture change could alter this constraint.

hypotheses.title: Cache keys should bind semantic projection, not mutable trust metadata
hypotheses.claim: Compiler/build-cache semantic keys should primarily bind BuildProjectionId plus compiler/runtime/backend semantic identity; mutable trust/freshness should gate cache use separately rather than poison semantic cache identity.
falsifiers: Cache reuse after trust state change violates required quarantine/security semantics even with a separate admissibility gate.
Compiler/backend nondeterminism requires additional inputs not captured by the proposed key.

counterhypotheses.claim: Manifest version ranges alone are sufficient for reproducibility.
Exact package version alone is a sufficient dependency identity.
One giant hash over manifest, resolver, trust, builder, graph and target is strictly better.
Current trust/yank/freshness verdict must be part of the immutable semantic graph identity.
A fetch mirror URL must be semantic identity.
A dependency can self-grant the effects it declares.
